name: How to Install and Test a Kitchen Sink and Faucet Assembly

step.name: Step 1: Shut off water valves and disconnect old fixtures
step.text: Close the hot and cold supply stops under the sink and turn on the faucet to release residual line pressure. Disconnect the flexible supply lines and unthread the drain P-trap over a bucket to catch standing water.

step.name: Step 2: Clean, prep, and check the countertop cutout
step.text: Remove the old sink and scrape away residual silicone or plumber's putty from the countertop deck. Clean the surface thoroughly and verify that your new sink basin fits the existing opening without binding against cabinet frames.

step.name: Step 3: Assemble the faucet and accessories on the sink deck
step.text: Mount the faucet body, sprayer hose, and soap dispenser onto the sink deck before setting the basin whenever possible. Ensure the base gasket or deck plate sits flat and secure the mounting hardware from underneath.

step.name: Step 4: Set the sink basin and connect the drain assembly
step.text: Apply the manufacturer-recommended sealant along the rim for drop-in sinks or secure mechanical brackets for undermount basins. Install the sink strainer baskets, reassemble the P-trap, and confirm drain pipes have proper slope toward the wall.

step.name: Step 5: Connect supply lines, flush the system, and test for leaks
step.text: Attach hot and cold braided lines to the shutoff valves and hand-tighten, finishing with a gentle wrench snug. Remove the faucet aerator, open water supplies, run both hot and cold lines for two minutes to flush line debris, reinstall the aerator, and inspect all connections with a dry cloth for slow drips.
